citations.desc: Access and inspection of records and property; submission of itineraries.
citations.narrative:
The licensee refused to allow USDA inspectors to conduct an inspection at approximately 12:30 PM. I spoke directly to
the licensee. My supervisor also spoke directly to the licensee by speaker phone. My supervisor and I both asked the
licensee multiple times if we could do an inspection. The licensee was busy with a move and would not accompany me
into his kennel to conduct an inspection. His original response was that he was too busy to accompany me on the
inspection. I explained to him what the possible consequences could be if he refused and encouraged him to do the
inspection with me. He tried to delay the inspection by up to two hours. My supervisor then directed me to leave and we
would have to cite it as a refusal.
Not allowing APHIS officials to conduct an inspection doesn't allow APHIS officials to ensure animal welfare standards are
being met. The licensee must allow APHIS officials to conduct an inspection when those officials show up to conduct an
inspection. Correct starting on 9/14/26.
No exit interview was conducted.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
